english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{11}=1$. For a real number $c$, let $L_c$ be the line $3x+4y=c$. Let $c_0<0$ be such that there is exactly one point on $L_{c_0}$ from which the two tangents drawn to $E$ are perpendicular to each other. Then the value of $c_0$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{11}=1$ है। किसी वास्तविक संख्या $c$ के लिए, माना $L_c$ रेखा $3x+4y=c$ है। माना $c_0<0$ ऐसा है कि $L_{c_0}$ पर ठीक एक ऐसा बिन्दु है जिससे $E$ पर खींची गई दोनों स्पर्श रेखाएँ परस्पर लम्बवत हैं। तब $c_0$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Points from which the tangents are perpendicular form the director circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}=36$
Exactly one such point on $L_c$ $\iff$ $L_c$ touches this circle: $\dfrac{|c|}{5}=6\Rightarrow c=\pm30$
solution_full: The tangent of slope $m$ to $E$ is $y=mx\pm\sqrt{25m^{2}+11}$. Through $(h,k)$: $(k-mh)^{2}=25m^{2}+11$, i.e. $(h^{2}-25)m^{2}-2hkm+k^{2}-11=0$.

The two tangents are perpendicular iff the product of the roots is $-1$: $\dfrac{k^{2}-11}{h^{2}-25}=-1$, i.e. $h^{2}+k^{2}=36$ (the director circle; the vertical-horizontal pairs from $(\pm5,\pm\sqrt{11})$ also lie on it).

So the required points of $L_c$ are its intersections with $x^{2}+y^{2}=36$. There is exactly one when $L_c$ is tangent to this circle: distance of the origin from $3x+4y=c$ equals $6$, $\dfrac{|c|}{5}=6$, $c=\pm30$.
originality_note: New: the director circle is used as a set and the line is made tangent to it, so 'exactly one point' becomes a distance condition (way 5). Closest known: equation of the director circle (a plain statement, listed as a known skeleton for circles). Different because: the question asks for a line parameter fixed by uniqueness, not for the circle itself. The ingredient is standard and the question is deliberately short (level 2).

Checked that both signs c = +-30 give one point and that c0 < 0 selects one; included the vertical/horizontal tangent case in the full solution. Changed: No change.
key_step: Perpendicular tangents come from the director circle x^2 + y^2 = 36; uniqueness means the line touches it.
justification: Two routine steps (director circle, tangency of a line to a circle) in numerical format; nothing unfamiliar. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 (L2), perpendicular tangents with a short finish.

concept_use.Director circle for Ellipse: The points from which the tangents to E are perpendicular form the director circle x^2 + y^2 = 36; the line has exactly one such point when it touches this circle.
